newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sees U.S. relations little changed.
newsitem.headline: Australia sees U.S. relations little changed.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton's election win was unlikely to affect Australia's relations with Washington, or Canberra's push to reinvigorate ties with the United States, a foreign ministry official said on Wednesday.

Prime Minister John Howard would not comment until the results of the senate and house elections were clearer, a spokesman said. But a foreign ministry official said Canberra expected little change in its relations with its close ally. "We don't expect things to be greatly different, it will be pretty much business as usual," the official told Reuters.
"The government will continue to maintain the United States as a high foreign policy priority," he said.
Labor opposition leader Kim Beazley welcomed Clinton's re-election ahead of his planned Australian visit this month.
"We look forward...to our bilateral relationship continuing to be based on mutual respect, common goals and, above all, close friendship," Beazley said in a statement.

Since ousting the 13-year-old Labor administration in March, Australia's conservative government has given priority to reinvigorating ties with Washington, a traditional ally Howard's administration says was neglected by Labor in favour of Asia. The two countries agreed to boost defence links during top-level talks in Sydney in July, in a move both said would buttress regional peace and security.

But Australia's moves towards closer ties with Washington has attracted criticism from Beijing, which has accused Australia of adopting a U.S. policy of containment towards China. Washington and Australia deny such a policy exists.
